    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the

answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure toward promotional_pricing, but that is the one direction inherited memory explicitly warns against: memory_73 is the most specific record we hold (+31% signups, -12% retention, weak PMF signal, standard SMB segment) and it directly contradicts the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Matching a price attack would likely reproduce that pattern, so I am not spending the single slot there.

Of the remaining directions, two address the actual observed decay rather than the competitor narrative: onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation down 6% QoQ. Onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a fix there plausibly relieves both; memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields produced a durable first-week activation lift) point the same way from two independent records, and memory_31 is the rare inherited claim that asserts durability rather than a one-week bump. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the close runner-up but only claims week-one engagement and a first meaningful action, which is a shallower and more easily gamed outcome. referral_incentive (memory_57) is explicitly scoped to established customers and does nothing for the self-serve funnel that is decaying. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is credible but addresses a segment that is not where the loss is showing.

I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 rather than on memory_73, because those two are the load-bearing support for what I intend to do and are stated in vague consolidated form with no effect sizes, sample sizes, or time horizons. memory_73 already carries enough specificity to act as a guardrail whether or not I verify it; a guardrail I am obeying is cheaper to leave unverified than a premise I am about to build on. Key things to check: whether memory_31's 'durable' lift was measured beyond week one, whether either result was confounded by concurrent changes, and whether memory_86's cohort resembles today's traffic mix, which the competitor may already have skewed toward lower-intent accounts.

Downstream value risk I want measured, not assumed away: cutting fields and steps can raise completion while lowering the quality of accounts that complete, and can strip data that sales and lifecycle systems depend on later. Completion rate is a proxy, not the objective. So this runs as a standard experiment with holdout, instrumented on retention and revenue quality at 30 and 60 days, not just on completion and week-one activation. Two consolidated priors plus a matching current-quarter signal justify a normal-sized test, not a broad rollout; if the archive shows either memory was a small, short-horizon, or confounded result, I would cut this to a small guarded test rather than proceed at this scale.
